what: T7, TABLE.md §6 ¶A and §7 — the inventory of every control the Band pane and the Structure pane offered at HEAD (v265, 3ce6125), with the home each one has in the Band table. Paul, 2026-09-03: 'get rid of everything it replaces. Move things around as needed. Don't lose unreplaced options. Find places for things and keep discoverability high.'
how: MEASURED, not read off the source: test/table-inventory.probe.js walked the rendered DOM of #pan-band and #pan-structure through all 36 states the two panes have (the roster, the crate, each voice x each of its four facets, the section list, each section's own questions, performance) at 390x844 and collected every button/select/input/[data-k]/[data-sel] in each. 72 control families, plus the two panes' own nav-tree children, which are controls too.
law: A home is (tier, where) — tier is row | column | cell | footer | table | elsewhere, and `reach` is the data-k the gate must find on the rendered table at 320px, tappable, at least 44px. `open` is what has to be tapped first to reach it (the sheet it lives in). A control with no home fails T7; so does a home that is not tap-reachable at 320.  ...AND `then` IS A LIST SINCE 2026-09-06 (TABLE.md §14). The seven record-scope surfaces are sections of ONE row now, so a control inside TIME is behind two doors and one inside the board's automation plate is behind three: `open` is the door a hand presses from rest and `then` is every door after it, in order. It was a single string for the one case that had two (the board's plates); a list is the same law counted honestly rather than a second field.
unmoved: 2026-09-05 (TABLE.md §13a.2): the three performance controls keep their addresses and move one door in — the PERFORM row is ONE LINE now (it was a row head beside a wrapping three-line strip of word plates, measured 92px on the Silence record at 390) and its three words are its FACE, so `performance.stress|phrase|orn` are in the sheet the row opens, with take, humanize and on time. Nothing is lost: `footCell` set `OPENFIELD` to an address the sheet it opened did not contain, so those three strips could not be opened at all.  2026-09-04 (wave 2c): the three performance sheets keep the address they had — `performance.stress|phrase|orn` — because an address does not move when a row does and three gates drive them by name. Wave 2b's first draft re-keyed them `tperf|<short>` for uniqueness inside the table; `tperf|` is gone from the page with that draft; the footer's other three fields (take, humanize, on time) already carried their own names.
renamed: 2026-09-04 (wave 2c): the Motif tab is `Motifs` (TABLE.md §8), so `tray-new`'s reach is `toptab-Motifs`. The HOME did not move — the bank still owns a motif's own editor — only the door's word; an inventory row is edited when its address is renamed and never when a control is lost.  ...AND TEN CONTROLS ARRIVED WITH THE SONIC SPREADSHEET (2026-09-05, TABLE.md §9a): the formula bar's head (taddr · tundo · tredo · tcopy · tpaste), the two clipboard verbs on the cell's own op bar, the column grip, and the two axis offers — which keep build-the-band's own addresses (tcol-add|line and trow-add), so the nine nav ops filed above still land on the controls they were filed onto.  ...AND THE NAV'S OP CHILDREN ARE GONE (2026-09-05, TABLE.md 9a: 'NO OP LIVES IN THE NAV: the tray keeps the Band tab and, at most, jump links'). addvoice/addbass/adddrums/addsec/secup/secdown/secdup/secdrop/dropvoice were all still drawn as tray rows beside the table homes filed here; the tray rows are deleted and the homes are unchanged, which is why not one `reach` in this file moved. What the stripe keeps is the JUMP: tab<voice> opens tcol|<voice> and secnav<id> opens trow|<id>, and neither has children. test/shell.js A6l and test/gutter.js shorten() drove the deleted branches by name and read the table's own ops in the same edit.  ...AND THE TWO `tadd|` ADDRESSES LASTED ONE AFTERNOON (2026-09-05, TABLE.md 13e). v288 filed `tadd|head` and `tadd|foot` as new — the two `+` cells, each opening an ADD sheet. Paul: "Don't pop up an interface when I add a section or a voice. Just add it." So a `+` now CARRIES the address of the op it fires (`tcol-add|<the first kind the band has not got>` at the head, `trow-add` at the foot) and writes on the tap; the two rows are deleted rather than re-pointed, because the button they filed is the button the offer's own row already files. NOTHING IS LOST AND NOTHING MOVED HOME: the four offers are at the addresses build-the-band minted, the three player kinds are all in every column head's sheet (`colOps`), and the `+` reaches the next of them the moment the one it offers exists.
moved: 2026-09-05 (TABLE.md §13f). Paul: 'Add chords below time and move chord stuff into it.' FIVE ROWS CHANGED HOME AND NOT ONE CHANGED ADDRESS: sel|alphabet.harmony, diatonic, the changes grid (prog<n>d / prog<n>i / sel|alphabet.quality|bar<n>), prog-add and prog-cut were filed under time-row and are filed under chords-row, behind `open: tchords` instead of `open: ttime`. Nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated: time-row goes from 17 rows to 12 and chords-row holds the 5, the TIME sheet no longer draws a changes grid or a harmony menu, and `goto.board` (record gain) stays in TIME as its back matter. Key, mode and scale stay in TIME because they are the alphabet a record counts WITH; the changes are what it does OVER them.
elsewhere: Two homes are outside the table on purpose and each says why: the Motifs bank owns a motif's own editor, and Where owns starting a record. Each is reached by ONE tap from the table, and the reach names that door. The SEAT is not one of them: it was filed as the board's in the first draft and test/sheets.js measured that wrong within the hour (zero insert seats on the whole page), so the voice's channel strip is drawn in its column sheet.

The seven record-scope surfaces — RULES, TIME, CHORDS, MOTIFS (the four rows above the grid) and MASTER, PRODUCE, PERFORMANCE (the three below it) — are the sections of one line at the top called THE RECORD, so every `open` that read `trules` / `ttime` / `tchords` / `tmotifs` / `tmix` / `tproduce` / `tfoot|perf` reads `trecord` now, with the row's own head first in `then`. WHAT IT COSTS, SAID PLAINLY: a record-scope control is TWO doors from rest where it was one, and the board's five plates are three where they were two. What it buys is measured in TABLE.md §14 — the head of the sheet goes from five rows to two and the foot from four to one, so the grid (the only surface that shows the whole song) starts 180px higher on a 390px phone. The MIX row did NOT move: a fader is the player's, so `tmix|<voice>` is still one door in the `<tfoot>`, aligned under its own column head.  AND EIGHT ROWS WHOSE `reach` IS A SCOPE HEAD ITSELF took `open: trecord` with no `then`: the head IS the control they were filed onto (the deleted Time / Rules / Mix / Motifs / Produce tabs, the performance tab, the rules axis jumps and the motif bank's `+`), so the door in front of them is the record row and there is nothing to open after it.
